title: Knowledge-Centred Verification Agent
summary: A claim-ledger-first verification framework for long legal, regulatory and financial documents. The ledger is the semantic source of truth and documents are rendered views of it. Work that needs judgment is separated from rules software can enforce, so a release gate is executable code rather than a model asked to reason harder.
evidence: eight executable rules in the first release: V-000, V-001, V-003, V-004, V-005, V-006D, V-008, V-024
claim_status vocabulary of eight states, from PENDING to UNRESOLVED
evidence_status vocabulary of six states, including LICENSE_REQUIRED and SOURCE_CONFLICT
two separate Finding contracts: compact validator findings and the richer protocol review Finding
V-010 and V-011 are declared unimplemented because Assumptions, Decisions and rendered spans are not yet validator inputs
the agent must declare external_retrieval = NO when authoritative retrieval is unavailable
friction: V-010 and V-011 were specified but could not be implemented, because Assumptions, Decisions and rendered spans are not yet modelled as validator inputs. Declaring them unimplemented was chosen over shipping a rule that appears to run and does not.
V-024 checks the Claim-level qualification only. Verifying it at every materially assertive rendered occurrence is what the protocol actually asks for, and that gap is recorded rather than glossed.
